title: Local cocycle classes for a general coefficient map in a commutative square
statement: Let $v:Z\to X$, $f:X\to S$, $k:Z\to T$ and $g:T\to S$ be scheme morphisms with $vf=kg$ [def-pc-scheme]. Fix modules $F$ on $X$, $G$ on $Z$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], a map $\varphi:F\to v_*G$ [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction], and $q\ge0$. Use the derived map $A(\varphi):Rf_*(F[0])\to Rg_*Rk_*(G[0])$ and right-adjoint mate comparison defined in [lem-weil-pbc-derived-square-unit-map]. Put $K=Rk_*(G[0])$. Suppose $e:H^q(Rg_*K)\to g_*H^q(K)$ is specified by the local equation $\Gamma(V,e)\Theta^{Rg_*K}_V=\Theta^K_{g^{-1}V}\lambda_{g,K,V}$ for every open $V\subseteq S$, where $\Theta$ is the canonical local-class map and $\lambda$ is the canonical inverse-open derived-sections comparison [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-top-edge]. For any such $V$, set $U=f^{-1}V$, $W=g^{-1}V$ and $U^{\prime}=v^{-1}U=k^{-1}W$. Restrict $\varphi$ to $\varphi_U:F|_U\to(v|_{U^{\prime}})_*(G|_{U^{\prime}})$ using the restriction adjunction and direct-image composition [def-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-open-choices]. Choose injective resolutions $I,J$ and augmentation-preserving restricted-resolution section identifications $R,R^{\prime}$ of that node. Let $\theta_V:H^q(U,F|_U)\to\Gamma(V,R^qf_*F)$ and $\theta^{\prime}_W:H^q(U^{\prime},G|_{U^{\prime}})\to\Gamma(W,R^qk_*G)$ be their canonical cocycle class maps [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-presheaf]. Transport $H^q(A(\varphi));e$ through the canonical total/classical derived comparisons and call the resulting map $a:R^qf_*F\to g_*R^qk_*G$. Then $\theta_V;\Gamma(V,a)=H^q(\varphi_U);\theta^{\prime}_W$, where $H^q(\varphi_U)$ is moduleCohomologyFMap [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]. No cohomological upper bound, flatness or derived pullback is assumed.

proof.text: Resolve F and G by I and J. Resolve v_*J by a bounded below complex L of injectives with quasi-isomorphism ell:v_*J -> L, and lift the coefficient map to beta:I -> L. The lift preserves the augmentation phi followed by v_* of the augmentation of J.

The existing derivedDirectImage_square_mate theorem identifies the right-adjoint mate with the canonical derived direct-image square. The existing normalizedDirectImageSquare_unit theorem computes its action on the pasted right-derived units. Apply these equations to the chosen injective representatives and beta,ell. They identify A(phi) with the roof f_*I -> f_*L <- g_*k_*J, whose arrows are f_*beta and f_*ell and whose underived square is the sectionwise direct-image square comparison.

Restrict to U and U-prime. Open restriction preserves injective resolutions and their augmentations. Sections of ell are a quasi-isomorphism; hence the cohomology of this roof is the cohomology map of the restricted coefficient map. The independence theorem allows exactly the specified restricted-resolution section comparisons.

The local class maps send each cocycle to its class in the cohomology sheaf. Apply their naturality to beta and ell and cancel only the section cohomology isomorphism induced by ell. The local derived-sections comparison and the defining equation of e identify the intermediate classes with inverse-open classes. The canonical total/classical comparisons and the augmentation-preserving resolution comparisons give the displayed equation.
